messages:
ryan-support: Hey team — customer 'AcmePayments' started seeing a spike of 429s this morning when they prefetch large contexts (64k). Happening only on the rw-64k-v2 variant. Errors show up after ~10s of processing, ~2xx->429. Any known per-model RPM/TPM or concurrency differences for the 64k variants?

lia-support: Thanks — can you paste a sample cURL + response body and the request-id from the error? Also which API key/org?

ryan-support: sample request: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-64k-v2","input":"<large prefetch>...","max_tokens":256,"context_length":65536}'``` response snippet: `{ "error": { "message": "rate limit exceeded", "type": "rate_limit", "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d" } }` Customer org: acme-pay, project: checkout.

lia-support: Received. A few quick checks: 1) Does this happen only with prefetch fanout (many concurrent upstream calls) or single-request large context? 2) Can you share the approximate RPS/RPM when the spike occurs?

ryan-support: It's prefetch fanout — their service fires 20 parallel prefetch calls per user session, each with ~60k context. Observed ~300 req/s during the spike, sustained for ~30s.

mike-sre: I pulled traces for `req_0a1b2c3d` — we see requests queueing at the front of the model pool and then being rejected by the per-model throttle before entering the runtime. Short burst window observed: auth passes, then rate gate returns 429. This looks like per-model burst/queue saturation rather than a global auth issue.

lia-support: Good catch. TL;DR guidance for customer: - implement client-side burst smoothing (token bucket / leaky bucket) - reduce simultaneous prefetch fanout (try 4–6 concurrent) - use exponential backoff with jitter on 429 - consider routing prefetch to a smaller-context model when possible

jamie-eng-runtime: Adding some detail: 64k model variants have tighter effective throughput due to memory/kv-cache pressure. We apply per-model RPM/TPM and max concurrency checks that can trigger earlier for large-context variants to protect SLAs. In this case, a short spike of many large-context requests trips the model's local queue and returns 429s as protective backpressure.

lia-support: For repro we created a small script to mimic their pattern — run this on a dev machine to reproduce: ```#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..20}; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-64k-v2","input":"$(head -c 60000 /dev/zero | tr '\\0' 'a')","max_tokens":10}' & done; wait``` If you run it with 20 parallel jobs you should see intermittent 429s within ~10–20s.

ryan-support: Repro works locally against staging with same pattern. Helpful to have the script. Customer is asking for concrete limits so they can tune — can we share ballpark numbers for rw-64k-v2?

jamie-eng-runtime: Ballpark (for operational guidance only, subject to change): rw-64k-v2 behaves like lower effective RPM/TPS compared to 8k models. Treat the 64k tier as ~1/4 to 1/6 the throughput of a standard 8k variant depending on sequence lengths. We prefer recommend testing with a scaled-down concurrency target rather than hard published numbers for now.

mike-sre: I'll open an internal ticket to look at short-burst admission tuning and whether we can provide better 429 headers (retry-after hints) for these cases. Ticket: INC-2026-4321, tagging @jamie-eng-runtime.

lia-support: Escalating to eng-runtime and SRE, and following up with the customer on suggested mitigations and the repro script. I'll attach traces and the request_id. @deploy-bot can you create a case with priority P2 for acme-pay?

deploy-bot: Case created: RWD-SUP-2026-0897 (P2) — assigned to lia-support.

ryan-support: Thanks everyone. I'll send the repro steps to the customer and advise smoothing their prefetch. If SRE/eng finds tuning options we can loop back and update them. :thumbsup:
